results.description: Ensure SMBv1 protocol is disabled (used by WannaCry/EternalBlue)
results.risk_explanation: SMBv1 is an insecure, legacy protocol vulnerable to remote code execution exploits like EternalBlue (used in the WannaCry ransomware attack). It lacks modern encryption and pre-authentication integrity checks.

results.description: Ensure User Account Control (UAC) is enabled
results.risk_explanation: Disabling UAC allows standard users and processes to silently elevate privileges and modify sensitive system files, registry entries, and core operating system configurations without administrative prompts.

results.description: Ensure RDP requires Network Level Authentication (NLA)
results.risk_explanation: Disabling Network Level Authentication (NLA) allows unauthenticated remote attackers to initiate RDP sessions before presenting credentials, exposing systems to credential brute-forcing, Denial of Service, and unauthenticated RCE exploits (e.g., BlueKeep CVE-2019-0708).

results.description: Ensure Windows Defender Real-Time Protection is active
results.risk_explanation: Disabling Defender real-time protection permits malware execution, malicious memory injections, and script-based droppers to run completely unhindered and undetected.

results.description: Ensure built-in Guest account is disabled
results.risk_explanation: An active Guest account provides anonymous local logon capability and can be leveraged by attackers for initial persistence or reconnaissance on the local network.

results.description: Ensure Windows Firewall is enabled for the Domain profile
results.risk_explanation: Disabling host-based firewalls for domain connections removes the first line of boundary defense against rogue endpoints, lateral network scans, and unauthorized service probing within corporate networks.

results.description: Ensure LSA Protection (RunAsPPL) is enabled to prevent credential dumping
results.risk_explanation: Running the Local Security Authority (LSA) process as a Protected Process Light (PPL) prevents non-protected processes, even those with administrative privileges, from injecting code or dumping credentials (e.g., Mimikatz reading lsass.exe memory).

results.description: Ensure PowerShell script execution policy is restricted
results.risk_explanation: An unrestricted PowerShell execution policy permits execution of unverified, downloaded scripts. Enforcing signed script execution or at least RemoteSigned prevents drive-by or downloaded malicious script execution.
results.remediation_command:
# CIS allows RemoteSigned; AllSigned is stricter but can break local dev scripts
Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope LocalMachine -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Force

results.description: Ensure Automatic Updates are not disabled via policy
results.risk_explanation: Disabling automatic updates prevents timely patching of critical zero-day vulnerabilities and OS security flaws, exposing the platform to known exploits documented in NVD/CVE databases.

results.description: Ensure BitLocker is fully encrypting the system drive (C:)
results.risk_explanation: Unencrypted volumes expose all host data, user credentials, and offline registry hives (SAM, SYSTEM) to physical theft, offline attacks, or malicious live booting.

results.description: Ensure AlwaysInstallElevated is disabled (HKLM) — prevents SYSTEM-level MSI install abuse
results.risk_explanation: When AlwaysInstallElevated is set to 1 in HKLM, Windows Installer executes all MSI packages with NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM privileges, allowing standard unprivileged users to craft a malicious MSI package and immediately gain full root/SYSTEM control.

results.description: Ensure AlwaysInstallElevated is disabled (HKCU)
results.risk_explanation: AlwaysInstallElevated in HKCU must also be 0; if enabled in conjunction with HKLM, standard users can trigger elevated MSI installations from their own user registry hive.

results.description: Ensure WDigest does not cache plaintext credentials in memory
results.risk_explanation: When UseLogonCredential is enabled (1), WDigest retains plaintext passwords in LSASS memory for digest authentication, allowing attackers with administrative access or memory inspection tools to extract cleartext passwords directly.

results.description: Ensure LLMNR (Link-Local Multicast Name Resolution) is disabled to prevent spoofing
results.risk_explanation: LLMNR allows unauthenticated multicast name queries on local subnets. Attackers on the same network use tools like Responder to poison LLMNR responses, tricking victims into sending NTLMv2 password hashes.
results.remediation_command: if (!(Test-Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\DNSClient')) { New-Item -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\DNSClient' -Force }; Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\DNSClient' -Name 'EnableMulticast' -Value 0 -Type DWord

results.description: Ensure AutoRun is disabled for all drives
results.risk_explanation: AutoRun / AutoPlay automatically executes programs from newly connected removable media (USB drives, CDs), serving as a common vector for physical and air-gap breaching malware (e.g., Stuxnet).

results.description: Ensure Windows Script Host (wscript/cscript) is disabled
results.risk_explanation: Windows Script Host (WSH) executes VBScript and JScript files (.vbs, .js). It is frequently abused by phishing attachments and initial access payloads to execute malicious code outside browser sandboxes.
results.remediation_command: if (!(Test-Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows Script Host\Settings')) { New-Item -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows Script Host\Settings' -Force }; Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows Script Host\Settings' -Name 'Enabled' -Value 0 -Type DWord

results.description: Ensure PowerShell Script Block Logging is enabled
results.risk_explanation: Without Script Block Logging (Event ID 4104), executed PowerShell code—including dynamically de-obfuscated commands and scripts loaded in-memory—is not recorded in event logs, blinding incident responders to malicious activity.

results.description: Ensure built-in Administrator account is disabled
results.risk_explanation: The built-in Administrator account has a well-known SID (RID 500) and is a primary target for password brute-forcing, password spray, and pass-the-hash attacks. It should be disabled in favor of named administrative accounts.

results.description: Ensure SMB client requires security signature
results.risk_explanation: Unsigned SMB traffic is vulnerable to Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) packet tampering and SMB Relay attacks, allowing adversaries to impersonate clients and execute commands on other domain systems.

results.description: Ensure Print Spooler service is stopped on non-print servers (PrintNightmare)
results.risk_explanation: The Windows Print Spooler service has a history of high-severity vulnerabilities (e.g. PrintNightmare CVE-2021-34527 / CVE-2021-1675) allowing remote code execution and local privilege escalation.
results.remediation_command:
# Apply to non-print servers only. If this host requires local printing, leave enabled
Stop-Service -Name Spooler -Force; Set-Service -Name Spooler -StartupType Disabled
